title: Fleet reset noise and driver symphony: field log
content:
Summary:
This is a field log capturing a recurring class of transient node resets across multiple racks during Feb–Mar 2028. Symptoms seen: short-lived kernel panics (0.5–4s), driver crash with NVIDIA modules unloading then reloading, NVLink link negotiation flaps, and short bursts of correctable ECC counts preceding the reset. Incidents are noisy (many small events) rather than a single catastrophic failure.

Why this doc exists (notes to self):
- Capture unusual timing/sequence patterns that aren't in the standard runbook.
- Record small experiments and temporary mitigations that we do in the lab before promoting to a runbook change.
- Surface telemetry gaps and quick wins for alerting.

Observed signal chain (typical trace from node X):
1) 90s of low-level ECC correctable spikes on mem-slab-3 (counts incrementing in bursts, not continuous).
2) 3–10s later nvlink0 reports "training: re-negotiation" in driver logs (multiple lanes).
3) Kernel OOPS with stack trace pointing at nvidia_uvm or nvidia_p2p (not always identical; sometimes shows dma mapping trace).
4) Systemd invokes nvidia-persistenced restart, driver modules unload and reload; node marks transient and most pods are rescheduled.
5) Soft quarantine (manual) stabilizes node for ~6–24 hours, then recurrence.

Key metrics and thresholds we pulled for triage: (these are shorthand for the metric names in our telemetry)
- gpu.ecc.correctable.count_bucketed (burst >200 in 60s)
- nvlink.retrain.count (any retrain >2 within 300s is suspicious)
- kernel.panic.rate (1 while other metrics spike)
- driver.reloads.per_hour (>=1 is noise)

Hypotheses so far (ordered by plausibility):
A) Thermal micro-fluctuation causing marginal signal integrity on NVLink retimers -> ECC bursts -> retrain -> driver race -> kernel panic.
  - Evidence: many nodes reporting small temp jumps on PMIC channel B at the same time as ECC bursts. Rack-level cooling cycles also correlate in 3 incidents.
B) Firmware mismatch between GPU microcode and host BIOS PCIe retimer firmware -> NVLink link negotiation corner cases.
  - Evidence: nodes with older NVRAM boot images exhibit more retrains.
C) Driver regression around memory fence ordering introduced in driver v536.x -> inconsistent teardown paths when NVLink retrains mid-stream.
  - Evidence: incidents spike shortly after we rolled driver v536.4 on a subset of Dedicated pools.
D) External EMI/noisy power rail causing transient voltage droops -> ECC bursts.
  - Evidence weak; power telemetry is noisy but not definitive.

Small lab experiments we ran (and quick outcomes):
- Reproduce: stress test (memtest-like + nvlink synthetic RPC) while toggling retimer clock gating. Result: we reproduced retrain step but not the kernel panic.
- Driver rollback: rolled nodes back to v535.7 on a canary pool (5 nodes) -> retrain events dropped by ~70% over 48h. Kernel panics on those nodes fell to 0.
- ECC scrub interval: increased proactive scrub interval (shorter) to clear correctable backlog -> transient correctable bursts reduced but retrains still occurred.
- Retimer firmware: flashed latest retimer image on 3 lab boards -> NVLink negotiation stabilized under load for those boards.

Immediate mitigations (what we did during on-call):
- Canary rollback of driver on newly affected Dedicated pools (JIRA-7891) — temporary, low-risk change.
- Automated soft-quarantine playbook: if driver.reloads.per_hour > 2 and ecc.correctable.burst>150 in 60s, mark node with tag "sre-transient-quarantine" and move critical pods.
- Increase ECC scrub frequency on fleet by factor 2 for 24 hours for affected racks.
- Engaged HW partner to schedule retimer firmware rollouts for highest-incident racks.

Longer-term actions (backlog and owners):
- eng-sre / eng-serving-runtime: design an NVLink retrain-aware driver watchdog that defers teardown if retrain in progress (owner: Diego; ETA: 2028-04-01).
- infra: standardize retimer firmware version as part of node configuration; prevent older images in autoscale pools (owner: Priya; ETA: 2028-04-15).
- observability: add a composite alert for "NVLink retrain chain" that considers ECC burst + retrain + driver reloads to reduce noise-to-signal (owner: Tomás; ETA: 2028-03-20).
- devtools: JIT tool to collect ephemeral kernel oops stacks and upload to a private bucket with automatic symbolization to speed triage (owner: Diego; spike started).

Telemety gaps / data we need:
- High-resolution retimer telemetry (we only have 30s granularity; need 1s during incidents).
- Persistent mapping from node -> retimer binary versions (some nodes boot with older NVRAM image; map is partial).
- Correlated datacenter power rail logs (PMIC traces) at 1s granularity for affected racks.

Runbook excerpt (draft wording to be folded into GPU instability runbook):
- Trigger: if ecc.correctable.burst > 150 in 60s AND nvlink.retrain.count >=2 in 5m -> escalate to on-call SRE and start soft-quarantine sequence.
- Immediate steps: gather kernel oops, capture dmesg, collect nvidia-smi -q --detailed, copy /var/log/nvidia* and /sys/devices/*/nvlink*/status, mark node unschedulable.
- Short-term remediation: rollback driver to last stable (pre-536.x) if that pool has recent regressions; otherwise, mark for retimer fw update.
- Postmortem hooks: correlate with rack cooling events and retimer fw version.

Open questions we still need answers to:
- Why do some nodes with identical hardware and firmware not show any retrain events? (config drift?)
- Is there a class of workload (large KV cache churn) that precipitates the sequence?
- Does increasing ECC scrub too aggressively mask a deeper underlying signal or actually help?

Notes to on-call engineers:
- Don’t immediately repro with heavy load on the same node — it can mask intermittent retrain windows. Try to collect data first.
- If you see nvlink retrain logs without ECC bursts, still snapshot retimer version; it might be a pure negotiation bug.
- Use the diagnostic script: /opt/sre/bin/gpu-nvlink-diagnostics.sh --collect-fast (uploads to incident bucket).

Appendix (quick reference commands):
- capture kernel logs: journalctl -k -b -1 > /tmp/kernel-btl-$(date +%s).log
- nvidia diagnostics: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION > /tmp/nvdiag.$(hostname).txt
- nvlink status: for d in /sys/class/nvlink/*; do echo $d; cat $d/status; done

TL;DR: Rolling back the driver reduced symptom frequency significantly in the short term; lab flashes of retimer firmware also improved stability. The chain appears to start from small ECC bursts that cascade into NVLink retrain events and then race conditions in the driver teardown. Next milestones: (1) better retimer firmware coverage, (2) composite alerting, (3) a retrain-aware defensive driver pattern.

Quick todo (for Monday):
- Diego: finish spike on retrain-aware watchdog (draft PR).
- Priya: inventory script for retimer firmware across fleet.
- Tomás: dashboard for composite NVLink retrain signal + alert rule proposition.

End of field log.
